class="article page no-article-survey" sc-render-smart-button="false" itemscope=""> <section class="article-container" data-stats-ve="35"><h1>Learn about smart features &amp; controls for Google Workspace &amp; other Google products</h1><div class="article-content-container"><div class="cc"><div></div>

<div class="note">
  <div>To give you more granular control over your data, we’ve updated our <a href="https://workspace.google.com/blog/product-announcements/updated-smart-feature-settings-give-users-increased-choice-and-control" rel="noopener" target="_blank">smart feature settings for Google Workspace</a>. This update turns the existing control into two distinct settings that govern different product experiences. These updates also give you more choice and control over your data, and do not alter our underlying data handling practices or our <a href="https://workspace.google.com/blog/identity-and-security/protecting-your-data-era-generative-ai" rel="noopener" target="_blank">robust privacy commitments</a>.</div>
</div>

<div><p>In Calendar, Chat, Drive, Gmail, Meet, and Voice, you can manage smart feature settings. Depending on your smart feature settings, you can do things like:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Use Gemini in Google Workspace to reference Drive files from Gmail.</li>
  <li>Automatically add events such as flights from Gmail to Calendar.</li>
  <li>Compile loyalty cards and tickets from your inbox into Google Wallet.</li>
  <li>Track an upcoming order using summary cards in Gmail.</li>
  <li>Record, transcribe, and summarize notes in Meet and Voice.</li>
</ul>

<h3 class="align-center"><a href="//www.youtube.com/watch?v=qCbsZ-j78cs" data-videoid="qCbsZ-j78cs" class="embedded-video-large"><span>Smart features &amp; controls for Google Workspace &amp; other Google products</span></a></h3>

<h3>In this article</h3>

<ul>
  <li><a href="15604322#smart_feature_settings_experiences" rel="noopener">Learn about smart feature settings &amp; experiences</a></li>
  <li><a href="15604322#how_smart_features_use_your_Google_Workspace_content_and_activity" rel="noopener">Learn how smart features use your Google Workspace content &amp; activity</a></li>
  <li><a href="15604322#change_smart_feature_settings" rel="noopener">Change smart feature settings</a></li>
  <li><a href="15604322#how_Google_handles_smart_feature_settings_data" rel="noopener">Learn how Google handles data in connection with smart feature settings</a></li>
</ul>
</div>

<div><h2><a id="smart_feature_settings_experiences" name="smart_feature_settings_experiences">Learn about smart feature settings &amp; experiences</a></h2>

<p>Each Workspace smart feature setting works independently from one another and provides different experiences. For example, you can turn on smart features for Google Workspace, and turn off smart features for other Google products. To understand how each smart feature setting works, use the table below.</p>

<table class="nice-table">
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>
      <p class="align-center"><strong>Smart feature setting</strong></p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p class="align-center"><strong>Where to find the setting</strong></p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p class="align-center"><strong>Description</strong></p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p class="align-center"><strong>Experience example</strong></p>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
      <p><a href="15604322#gcm" rel="noopener"><strong>Smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet</strong></a></p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p>Gmail</p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p>Controls use of your Gmail, Chat, and Meet data to provide smart features for these products.</p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p>Smart Compose in Gmail</p>

      <p>Summary cards</p>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>
      <p><a href="15604322#gw" rel="noopener"><strong>Smart features in Google Workspace</strong></a></p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p>Gmail</p>

      <p>Calendar*</p>

      <p>Chat*</p>

      <p>Drive*</p>

      <p>Meet*</p>

      <p>Voice*</p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p>Controls use of your Workspace data to provide smart features across Workspace products.</p>

      <p>This setting does not affect smart features that personalize your experience in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, which are subject to the control described above.</p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p>Show events from Gmail in Calendar, such as flight itineraries and invitations</p>

      <p>Google Workspace with Gemini</p>
      </td>
    </tr>

      <td>

      </td>
      <td>
      <p>Gmail</p>

      <p>Calendar*</p>

      <p>Chat*</p>

      <p>Drive*</p>

      <p>Meet*</p>

      <p>Voice*</p>
      </td>
      <td>
      <p><span>Controls use of your Workspace data to provide smart features in other Google products.</span></p>

      <p><span>Data sharing and personalization in certain Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as <a href="/websearch/answer/54068?hl=en&amp;co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid" rel="noopener">Web and App Activity</a> and <a href="/accounts/answer/14202510" rel="noopener">DMA linked services</a> (in the EU).</span></p>
      </td>

      <p>Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)</p>
      </td>

<p>* You can only turn on this setting from a web browser.</p>
</div>

<div><a class="zippy" id="gcm" name="gcm">Smart features in Gmail, Chat &amp; Meet</a>
<div>
  <p>When you turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, you agree to let Gmail, Chat and Meet use your content and activity in these products to personalize your experience in those apps.</p>

  <p>When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in Gmail, Chat and Meet that include:</p>

  <ul>
    <li><a href="/mail/answer/3094499" rel="noopener">Automatic email filtering / categorization (Primary/Social/Promotions)</a></li>
    <li><a href="/mail/answer/9116836" rel="noopener">Smart Compose (suggested text) in email</a></li>
    <li><a href="/mail/answer/17493601" rel="noopener">Smart Reply (suggested quick replies) in email</a></li>
    <li><a href="/mail/answer/15195630" rel="noopener">Summary cards above emails (travel, package tracking, and more)</a></li>
  </ul>

  <p>The setting controls app-level smart features which personalize your experience within Gmail, Chat, or Meet. Changes to this setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Google Workspace setting.</p>

  <p>When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Gmail, Chat, and Meet. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.</p>

  <p>Even if you turn off smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, some smart features with individual on and off settings are still available. Some examples include:</p>

  <ul>
    <li><a href="/chat/answer/12918975" rel="noopener">Conversation summaries in Chat</a></li>
    <li><a href="/chat/answer/7654374" rel="noopener">Smart Reply in Chat</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
<a class="zippy" id="gw" name="gw">Smart features in Google Workspace</a>

<div>
  <p>When you turn on smart features in Google Workspace, you agree to let Google Workspace use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience across Workspace. Workspace includes apps for businesses and schools, such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more. To learn more, visit the <a href="https://workspace.google.com/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Workspace website</a>.</p>

  <p>When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences across Workspace that include:</p>

  <ul>
    <li>Show events from Gmail in Calendar (<a href="/calendar/answer/6084018" rel="noopener">such as flight itineraries and invitations</a>).</li>
    <li>Personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results) in products like <a href="/drive/answer/2375114" rel="noopener">Drive</a>.</li>
    <li>Ask Gemini to summarize content, create drafts, and find key information, along with <a href="/mail/answer/13952129" rel="noopener">other Google Workspace with Gemini features</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <p>When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Google Workspace products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.</p>

  <p>Changes to the smart features in Google Workspace setting don't affect your existing control over the smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet setting described above.</p>
</div>
<a class="zippy" id="ogp" name="ogp">Smart features in other Google products</a>

<div>
  <p>When you turn on smart features in other Google products, you agree to let Google use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience in other Google products.</p>

  <p>When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in other Google products that include:</p>

  <ul>
    <li><a href="/maps/answer/3503748" rel="noopener">Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only)</a></li>
    <li><a href="/wallet/answer/12060038#zippy=%2Cadd-items-from-gmail" rel="noopener">Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)</a></li>
    <li><a href="/gemini/answer/16598406" rel="noopener">Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app (personal accounts only)</a></li>
    <li><a href="/websearch/answer/16859283" rel="noopener">Personal Intelligence in Search services (personal accounts only)</a></li>
  </ul>

  <p>When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in other Google products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.</p>

  <p>In addition, data sharing and personalization in other Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as <a href="/websearch/answer/54068?hl=en&amp;co=GENIE.Platform%3DAndroid" rel="noopener">Web and App Activity</a> and <a href="/accounts/answer/14202510" rel="noopener">DMA linked services</a> (in the EU).</p>

  <p>Even when the setting for smart features in other Google products is turned off, if you choose to share your Workspace data through screen actions (including screenshots), some smart features in other Google products will still be available. An example is when you <a href="/gemini/answer/15850607" rel="noopener">use screen actions to chat with Gemini Apps</a>.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div><h2><a id="how_smart_features_use_your_Google_Workspace_content_and_activity" name="how_smart_features_use_your_Google_Workspace_content_and_activity">Learn how smart features use your Google Workspace content &amp; activity</a></h2>

<p><strong>Important:</strong> By default, smart feature settings are off if you live in:</p>

<ul>
  <li>The European Economic Area</li>
  <li>Japan</li>
  <li>Switzerland</li>
  <li>United Kingdom</li>
</ul>

<p></p>

<p>When smart features are on, your data may be used to improve these features. Across Google and Workspace, we’ve long shared robust <a href="https://workspace.google.com/blog/identity-and-security/protecting-your-data-era-generative-ai?e=48754805" rel="noopener" target="_blank">privacy commitments that outline how we protect user data and prioritize privacy</a>. Generative AI doesn’t change these commitments — it actually reaffirms their importance. <a href="14615114" rel="noopener">Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet &amp; Vids protects your data</a>.</p>
</div>

<div><h2><a id="change_smart_feature_settings" name="change_smart_feature_settings">Change smart feature settings</a></h2>

<p>Learn how to change your smart feature settings in different Google Workspace products. You can change smart feature settings on your computer or in the Gmail app for Android, iPhone, or iPad.</p>
</div>

<gkms-context-selector id="15604486"></gkms-context-selector><h3>Change smart feature settings for Gmail, Chat &amp; Meet</h3>

<p><strong>Important</strong>: Changes to smart feature settings apply across all devices and apps where you’re signed in.</p>

<ul>
  <li>If you’re on the mobile Gmail app but don’t get a notification about the changes, update your app.</li>
  <li>Some changes made on your computer don’t reflect in the mobile app.</li>
</ul>

<ol>
  <li>On your computer, go to <a href="https://mail.google.com/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Gmail</a>.</li>
  <li>At the top right, click Settings <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU"> <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="and then" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw"> <strong>See all settings</strong>.</li>
  <li>In the “General” tab, scroll to “Smart features.”</li>
  <li>Next to “Turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet,” check or uncheck the box.</li>
</ol>

<h3>Change smart feature settings for Google Workspace &amp; other Google products</h3>

<h4>Gmail</h4>

<ol>
  <li>On your computer, go to <a href="https://mail.google.com/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Gmail</a>.</li>
  <li>At the top right, click Settings <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU"> <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="and then" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw"> <strong>See all settings</strong>.</li>
  <li>Under the “General” tab, scroll to “Google Workspace smart features.”</li>
  <li>Click <strong>Manage Workspace smart feature settings</strong>.</li>
  <li>Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Smart features in Google Workspace</strong></li>
      <li><strong>Smart features in other Google products</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>At the bottom right, click <strong>Save</strong>.</li>
</ol>

<h4>Google Calendar</h4>

<ol>
  <li>On your computer, go to <a href="https://calendar.google.com/calendar/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Calendar</a>.</li>
  <li>At the top right, click Settings <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU"> <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="and then" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw"> <strong>Settings</strong>.</li>
  <li>Under "General," click <strong>Google Workspace smart features</strong> <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="and then" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw"> <strong>Manage Workspace smart features settings</strong>.</li>
  <li>Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Smart features in Google Workspace</strong></li>
      <li><strong>Smart features in other Google products</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>At the bottom right, click <strong>Save</strong>.</li>
</ol>

<h4>Google Chat</h4>

<ol>
  <li>On your computer, go to <a href="https://chat.google.com" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Chat</a>.</li>
  <li>At the top right, click Settings <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU"> <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="and then" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw"> <strong>Data Privacy</strong>.</li>
  <li>Under "Google Workspace smart features," click <strong>Manage settings</strong>.</li>
  <li>Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Smart features in Google Workspace</strong></li>
      <li><strong>Smart features in other Google products</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>At the bottom right, click <strong>Save</strong>.</li>
</ol>

<h4>Google Drive</h4>

<ol>
  <li>On your computer, go to <a href="https://drive.google.com" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Drive</a>.</li>
  <li>At the top right, click Settings <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU"> <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="and then" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw"> <strong>Settings</strong>.</li>
  <li>Click <strong>Privacy</strong>.</li>
  <li>Click <strong>Manage Workspace smart feature settings</strong>.</li>
  <li>Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Smart features in Google Workspace</strong></li>
      <li><strong>Smart features in other Google products</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>At the bottom right, click <strong>Save</strong>.</li>
</ol>

<h4>Google Meet</h4>

<ol>
  <li>On your computer, go to <a href="http://meet.google.com/" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Meet</a>.</li>
  <li>At the top right, click Settings <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/5neVYO8C6nKfsUhkI7y46Vsv-pHctH91nQk4Tl5inR_9Lo3ga5nKq6jeOlrcPE4DBNU"> <img src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw=h36" width="auto" height="18" alt="and then" data-mime-type="image/png" data-alt-src="//lh3.googleusercontent.com/3_l97rr0GvhSP2XV5OoCkV2ZDTIisAOczrSdzNCBxhIKWrjXjHucxNwocghoUa39gw"> <strong>General</strong>.</li>
  <li>Next to "Google Workspace smart features," click <strong>Manage</strong>.</li>
  <li>Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Smart features in Google Workspace</strong></li>
      <li><strong>Smart features in other Google products</strong></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>At the bottom right, click <strong>Save</strong>.</li>
</ol>


<div><h2><a id="how_Google_handles_smart_feature_settings_data" name="how_Google_handles_smart_feature_settings_data">Learn how Google handles data in connection with smart feature settings</a></h2>

<p>If you have a personal Google Account, this notice and our <a href="https://policies.google.com/privacy" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Privacy Policy</a> describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.</p>

<p>If you have a work or school Google Account, this notice and the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/terms/cloud-privacy-notice" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Google Cloud Privacy Notice</a> describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.</p>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><a class="zippy zippy-expand">What are Google’s legal bases of processing for users in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland?</a>
<div>
  <p>For users based in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland, Google processes your information for the purposes, and on the legal grounds, described below.</p>

  <p>When we refer to “your Workspace Content &amp; Activity” below, we mean content from Workspace apps such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more, and related data about how you use Workspace products.</p>

  <p>Google’s legal bases are:</p>

  <ul>
    <li><strong>Your consent</strong>. We rely on your consent for Google to use your Workspace Content &amp; Activity, when you turn on any of the smart features settings for Google Workspace, for the following purposes:

      <ul>
        <li><strong>To provide smart features that personalize your experience in Gmail, Chat and Meet</strong>. For example, when you turn the smart features in Gmail, Chat and Meet setting on, you can get experiences that include Gmail Smart Compose (suggested text in email).</li>
        <li><strong>To provide smart features that personalize your experience across Google Workspace</strong>. For example, when you turn the smart features in Google Workspace setting on, you can get experiences that include personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results). This setting does not affect your control over the smart features setting that personalizes your experience in Gmail, Chat, and Meet.</li>
        <li><strong>To provide smart features that personalize your experience in other Google products outside of Workspace</strong>. For example, when you turn the smart features in other Google products setting on, you can get experiences that include restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps. Data sharing and personalization in certain products may be subject to additional controls such Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).</li>
      </ul>

      <p>You can revoke your consent to any of these purposes at any time by turning off the relevant setting as described in the “Change smart feature settings” section above.</p>
    </li>
    <li><strong>Google and </strong><strong>third parties' legitimate interests</strong><strong> with appropriate safeguards to protect your privacy.</strong>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>To improve our services</strong>. If you have turned on any of the smart features settings, we may also process your Workspace Content &amp; Activity to improve these features.
          <p>Processing information for this purpose is necessary for the legitimate interests of Google and our users in:</p>

          <ul>
            <li>Providing, maintaining and improving services for our users (such as a flight confirmation email you receive being used to create a summary card that appears in your Gmail).</li>
            <li>Developing new products and features that are useful for our customers and users (for example, processing aggregated Gmail data helped us develop and launch Smart Compose suggestions as you enter text in Gmail).</li>
            <li>Performing research that benefits our users and the public (such as to conduct a user study that helped us develop and launch Smart Reply suggested responses in Gmail).</li>
          </ul>

          <p><a href="https://workspace.google.com/blog/identity-and-security/protecting-your-data-era-generative-ai?e=48754805" rel="noopener" target="_blank">Learn more about how we’re protecting your Google Workspace data in the era of generative AI</a>.</p>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </li>
  </ul>
</div>
</div>

<div class="no-margin"><a class="zippy zippy-expand">How long is your Workspace Content &amp; Activity used to provide smart features and to improve these features?</a>
<div>
  <p>Your Workspace Content &amp; Activity is used to provide you with smart features as long as the relevant smart feature setting is turned on. Turning off a smart feature setting or deleting your Workspace Content &amp; Activity stops that data from being used to provide relevant smart features to you in the future.</p>

  <p>Turning off a smart feature setting means your Workspace Content &amp; Activity will no longer be used to improve the relevant smart features moving forward. The learnings developed from this improvement process may persist even after you turn off a smart feature setting or delete your Workspace Content &amp; Activity from your Google Account. However, turning off a smart feature setting means that your Workspace Content &amp; Activity would no longer be actively processed to improve the relevant smart features after you have turned the setting off.</p>
</div>
</div>
